miniPosts.title: The Hidden Courtyards of Berlin: A Walk Through the Höfe Around Hackescher Markt
miniPosts.summary: Behind the facades around Hackescher Markt, Berlin hides a second layer: connected inner courtyards, the Höfe, that most visitors walk straight past. Here is which passages to step into and in what order, from the tiled Hackesche Höfe to a street-art courtyard, a rose garden and a hand-made candy workshop, all within a ten-minute walk.
miniPosts.alt: The illuminated Art Nouveau tiled facade of the first courtyard of the Hackesche Höfe in Berlin at night.

miniPosts.title: Telling Time in German: Why Halb Acht Is 7:30 and How Berlin Says the Rest
miniPosts.summary: Somebody says halb acht, you arrive at half past eight, and the table is gone. Berlin runs two clocks at once: everything written uses 24 hours, and almost everything spoken drops back to twelve and then counts towards the hour that has not arrived yet. Here is the one shift that makes German time make sense, the eastern viertel and dreiviertel forms you will hear around Berlin, the day codes on a museum door, and a dial you can turn to test all of it.
miniPosts.alt: The Urania World Clock on Alexanderplatz in Berlin, its metal cylinder marked with world cities above a lit band of hour numbers running past 12, 13, 14 and 15.
